subject: Surgery
title: Acute Appendicitis: Alvarado Score & Imaging
preview: Appendicitis is evaluated using the clinical pattern, serial examination, laboratory context and appropriate imaging.

sections.title: Clinical features
points: Pain often begins centrally and localizes to the right lower abdomen; nausea, anorexia and focal tenderness may occur.
Elderly, pregnant and immunosuppressed patients can have atypical findings.

sections.title: Investigation pathway
points: Combine examination, blood tests and appropriately selected ultrasound or cross-sectional imaging.
Consider gynecologic, urinary and gastrointestinal mimics when evaluating right lower-quadrant pain.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Do not diagnose or exclude appendicitis from a single fever cutoff or Alvarado point total.
Worsening pain, systemic instability or peritoneal signs require urgent reassessment.

quickRevision: Migrating periumbilical-to-right-lower-quadrant pain is classic, but presentations are variable.
Clinical scores such as Alvarado can assist risk stratification; they are not independent proof of appendicitis.
Imaging selection depends on age, pregnancy, probability and local expertise.

quiz.question: Which finding makes appendicitis assessment more concerning?
options: Migrating pain to right lower quadrant with local tenderness
quiz.explanation: Migrating pain to right lower quadrant with local tenderness. • Rovsing's Sign: Palpation of Left Lower Quadrant causes pain in Right Lower Quadrant.
